extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians/authors preparing manuscripts for Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle's Journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Author guidelines for preparing and submitting research articles to Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle's Journal), covering required metadata, formatting, language, and publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route and adherence to Information for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit your paper via our online submission system accessible here, following the Information for Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the journal's online submission system and the detailed 'Information for Authors' linked from the submission page; consult the editor if in doubt before sending an electronic manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and Mathematics Subject Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper should include a short but informative abstract, as well as the Mathematics Subject Classification 2010 representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise informative abstract and list MSC 2010 codes (primary and secondary) so the editorial office and reviewers can quickly see the article's subject classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred typesetting system
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate the publication process, authors are encouraged to submit the final manuscript typed using plain TEX or one of its derivatives. Please download the class file here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain TeX/LaTeX (the provided class file) for final manuscripts to speed production; if unsure about formatting details, consult the editor prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: General style: traditional Crelle presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Crelle's Journal follows the traditional style of presentation and layout that has been part of this journal since its inception. This applies to formulas, references and other. Our copyediting will help you with adapting your accepted manuscripts to the Crelle style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should format manuscripts in the traditional style (as exemplified in the journal); copyediting will adjust accepted papers to the house style, but initial adherence helps avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title content and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: In the title formulas or mathematical symbols should be avoided, if possible, or kept to a minimum. Only the first word and proper nouns should be capitalized. If the title is long, a shortened version should be supplied for the running heads, which together with the author’s name should not exceed 80 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid heavy use of symbols in the title; use sentence-style capitalization (only first word and proper nouns). Supply a short running head if needed so that 'running head + author name' stay within 80 characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of theorem-like proclamations (Theorem, Lemma, Proposition, Corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proclamations such as Proposition, Theorem, Lemma, Corollary are set in boldface, followed by the text in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark theorem-like environments with boldface headings and place the statement text in italics to match the journal's typographical conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of remark-like proclamations (Remark, Definition, Example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proclamations such as Remark, Definition, Example are set in boldface, but followed by the text in Roman (not italic) typeface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use boldface for the environment label (Remark/Definition/Example) and set the ensuing text in normal roman type (not italics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals in mathematical expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerals in mathematical expressions should always be Roman
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When typesetting numerals inside mathematical expressions follow the journal's rule to use Roman font for numerals (preserve their stated instruction exactly); consult class file/examples for the intended usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of displayed formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering of displayed formulas is flush left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place equation numbers at the left margin (flush left) according to the journal's display-numbering convention rather than the more common right-side numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes should be numbered consecutively and placed at the foot of the page to which they refer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number footnotes in sequence through the paper and ensure each footnote appears at the bottom of the page containing its reference, not collected elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: alphabetical listing and citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be listed alphabetically and conform to the following example: [3] H. Hasse, Symmetrische Matrizen im Körper der reellen Zahlen, J. reine angew. Math. 153 (1923), 12–43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List bibliography alphabetically by author and format entries to match the provided example (journal abbreviation, volume, year, page range). Use the class file or journal examples for precise punctuation and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of authors' addresses and contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors’ addresses should appear at the end of the manuscript, following the list of references. An e-mail address should be included if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the references include full author affiliations/addresses and an email address when available, conforming to the journal's end-matter placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted manuscript languages and language checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts of articles should be in English, French or German. Authors whose native language is not English, French or German are asked to have their article carefully checked by a native speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit in one of the three allowed languages and, if not a native speaker, have the text reviewed by a native speaker to avoid language-based desk rejection or delays in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with publication ethics and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a paper please get familiar with our Publication Ethics and Malpractice Statement as well as Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the journal's ethical policies and copyright terms prior to submission to ensure compliance with authorship, conflicts of interest, originality, and copyright transfer/open-access choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository policy for author distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Our repository policy allows you to distribute 30 PDF copies of your published article to colleagues (the PDF has to include the information that it is an author's copy). Please also feel free to distribute the link to the online abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may share up to 30 PDFs marked as 'author's copy' and circulate the abstract link freely; follow the stated repository policy restrictions when sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid open access option and transformative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: In this journal, authors have the option to publish their article under an open access license. Please note that authors from institutions with which we have a transformative agreement can publish open access without paying an article processing charge (APC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the hybrid OA option; check whether your institution has a transformative agreement to avoid APCs and consult the 'Funding and Support' information for eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged use of provided LaTeX class file
rubrics_metrics.description: Please download the class file here. If in doubt, please consult the editor concerning details before sending an electronic manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal's provided class/style file to ensure compliance with typographical conventions; contact the editor with formatting questions pre-submission to prevent avoidable production edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author benefits of publishing (visibility & archiving)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your benefits of publishing with us: Fast access to articles due to ahead of print publishing; High Impact Factor; Mathematical Citation Quotient; Every article easily discoverable because of Search Engine Optimization (SEO) and comprehensive abstracting and indexing services; Convenient citation tracking via e-mail alert; Secure archiving by De Gruyter and Portico; Professional sales and marketing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are stated advantages to publishing in the journal (visibility, indexing, archiving); authors should be aware of these practical benefits when choosing where to submit.
